clue.text: Friends returning fancy new shirt to get a reprimand

indicators.note: returning means the word for friends comes back the other way

parts.note: pals are friends

indicators.note: fancy as a verb or adjective suggests something elaborated or reimagined, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Mates hand back a smart new shirt, and somebody gets told off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' and 'fancy' are both at work: the first reverses the synonym for friends, the second scrambles the words that follow it. The definition is just 'reprimand', with 'to get a' as link.
explanation.definitionFit: A light telling-off is idiomatically described this way, as if a mild smack on the hand.

clue.text: Full dataset crashed after one entry

indicators.note: entry means a piece is let into the middle of the other letters
a crashed set of data is scrambled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A computer file that is full to bursting crashes after one more record is added.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashed' turns DATASET into SATATED; 'entry' puts I (one) inside to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being satisfied to the point of having had enough is being full.

clue.text: Wrong time to upset a Cornishman

indicators.note: upset suggests knocked over and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Picking the wrong moment to annoy a man from Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges A CORNISHMAN. Cornwall is the county at the far south-western tip of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Something placed in the wrong period, out of its era, is a chronological error.

clue.text: Operation in which revolutionary Green Party hero welcomes us back

indicators.note: welcomes means one group of letters takes the other in among them
revolutionary suggests overturning, so the letters of Green Party hero are rearranged
back means the word us is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A radical environmentalist champion embraces our cause again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' looks like it describes the hero but is the anagram signal; 'back' reverses US, which 'welcomes' puts inside the scramble.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgery on the cardiac organ with the chest opened is a major medical procedure, which is an operation.

clue.text: See 1 across
The man's fear of Spain

parts.note: belonging to the man is his
panic is sudden fear

explanation.surface: A fellow's dread of the Iberian country.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes something Spanish or Spanish-speaking, i.e. belonging to Spain.

clue.text: Friendly princes love to enter record of conflict

parts.note: warm means friendly

indicators.note: to enter means one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: emirs are Arab princes
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Amiable royals let love into their lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to enter' puts O (love, a zero score in tennis) inside EMIRS to make EMOIRS.
explanation.definitionFit: Personal written accounts of battle are a record of fighting.

clue.text: Goliath said to be wise a very long time ago

parts.note: the setter Goliath refers to himself as I

indicators.note: said means the words are spoken, so we go by how they sound run together

parts.note: sage as an adjective means wise; run on after I, it is heard as the rest of the phrase

explanation.surface: The setter is reputed to have been clever in the distant past.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, I SAGE runs together as the answer, so the S of SAGE is heard as the end of ICE. Setters often use their pseudonym for I or ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A glacial period lies in the remote prehistoric past, standing for an era long ago.

clue.text: Judging is difficult

definitions.meaning: ... a case in court is judging it
a ... situation is a hard one

explanation.definitionFit: Hearing a court case is trying it, and a trying day is a hard, wearing one.

clue.text: See 3
Swing role reversal with reported ease

indicators.note: reversal means the word for role is turned backwards

parts.note: a part is an actor's role

indicators.note: reported means we hear the word ease spoken

parts.note: the word ease sounds like the letters EZE

explanation.surface: A swing-voter's change of heart, accomplished with apparent ease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversal' turns PART into TRAP; 'reported' gives EZE, which sounds like 'ease'.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus swing hung high for acrobats is this apparatus.

clue.text: See 3
Long for bachelor part

indicators.note: part means only a portion of the word bachelor is used

explanation.surface: A single man yearning for a role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' points to a run of letters inside bACHElor.
explanation.definitionFit: To yearn is to long, as in aching for home.

clue.text: Equip old fellow with weapons for the big battle

parts.note: to arm is to equip with weapons
aged means old
a don is a college fellow

explanation.surface: Supplying an elderly man with guns for the final showdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with weapons' completes the sense of 'Equip' (to arm is to equip with weapons) wrapped round the other pieces in the surface. A DON is a university fellow at Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical last conflict between good and evil has become a byword for a huge, decisive war.

clue.text: At the earliest opportunity, instead of mucking around, hearing nothing

indicators.note: around means the scrambled letters go round the other piece
mucking about suggests messing things up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the phrase is read as in stead of, so the letters of stead of are the fodder
ASAP abbreviates as soon as possible

explanation.surface: Someone told to stop fooling about at once simply cannot hear the order.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'instead' as 'in stead': 'mucking' rearranges STEAD OF into DEAFOST, and 'around' wraps it round ASAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Being totally deaf, unable to hear a thing, is likened in this idiom to a lifeless wooden pole.

clue.text: Perhaps Jeremy Clarkson's skill with language finally appearing in favourite highway

parts.note: a pet is a favourite

indicators.note: appearing in means these letters go inside the other word

parts.note: a road is a highway

indicators.note: finally means take the last letter of each of these words

explanation.surface: A TV presenter's way with words is finally on show on his beloved motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes L, H and E from 'skill with language'; 'appearing in' puts them inside ROAD. Jeremy Clarkson is a British TV presenter famous for car shows such as Top Gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A car enthusiast is slangily called this, and the motoring presenter is a famous example.

clue.text: Brought to mind the night before, eating fine dinner starter

indicators.note: eating means one word swallows the other

parts.note: eve is the evening before an event
OK means fine

indicators.note: starter means the first letter of dinner

explanation.surface: Recalled the previous evening, which began with a good meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the night before' is EVE, as in Christmas Eve; 'eating' and 'starter' are both indicators, a container and a first-letter pick.
explanation.definitionFit: To call up a memory or feeling is to summon it to the mind.

clue.text: Note to dignitary: backtracking is essential

indicators.note: backtracking means the whole sequence is read from end to start

parts.note: la is a note of the sol-fa scale
a VIP is a very important person

explanation.surface: A memo to an important figure saying that retreating is necessary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backtracking' turns the whole run of three pieces round, not just one. The colon in the surface is only punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: Something crucial, on which all else turns, is vital.

clue.text: Same style after standard northern cheese

indicators.note: after means the rearranged letters follow the word for standard

parts.note: par is the standard level

indicators.note: style suggests reshaping, so the letters of Same are rearranged

explanation.surface: A northern cheese made in a familiar way to the usual standard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'style' is the anagram signal on 'Same', and 'after' puts that scramble following the golf term for standard. The definition 'cheese' sits at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard Italian grating type from around Parma is a well-known cheese.

clue.text: Inspect ship's make-up

parts.note: to eye something is to inspect it
a liner is a passenger ship

explanation.surface: Examining a vessel's paint job.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmetic for outlining the lids is a kind of make-up.

clue.text: Being 14, see what people say

parts.note: 14 down describes someone who cannot hear, and such a person follows speech by watching the mouth

explanation.definitionFit: Reading speech from mouth movements is how someone who cannot hear follows what is said.

clue.text: Tea brewed in attempt to reach agreement

indicators.note: in means the rearranged letters go inside the word for attempt

parts.note: a try is an attempt

indicators.note: brewed suggests stewing and mixing, so the letters of Tea are rearranged

explanation.surface: Diplomats make tea while trying to strike a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewed' turns TEA into EAT, put 'in' TRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal pact between states is an agreement.

clue.text: Inspired by Volkswagen's car: a beautiful Beetle

indicators.note: inspired by means the letters are breathed in by, so held within, the words that follow

explanation.surface: Admiring the lovely Beetle model from the German car maker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspired by' points to letters held inside volkswageN'S CAR A Beautiful. The Beetle in the surface is the VW car; the definition means the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The sacred dung beetle of ancient Egypt is a type of the insect.

clue.text: Working subject said to be modern and available

parts.note: on means working, as a machine is on
a theme is a subject

indicators.note: said means the word is heard, not seen

parts.note: new means modern; spoken it sounds like the letters NU

explanation.surface: An up-to-date topic is under discussion and ready to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' gives NU, which sounds like NEW (modern).
explanation.definitionFit: Offered for ordering in a restaurant, figuratively something up for choice and so obtainable.

clue.text: Heard praise in addition

indicators.note: heard means the word for praise is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a compliment is an expression of praise

explanation.surface: Hearing words of admiration as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heard' points to a word that sounds like the one meaning praise but is spelt with an E.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that completes or adds to a whole is an extra amount added.

clue.text: High-rise alarmed middle class right-wing Englanders

indicators.note: high suggests intoxicated and out of order, so the letters of rise alarmed are rearranged

explanation.surface: Suburban conservatives are horrified at a tower block.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High' rearranges RISE ALARMED. The Daily Mail is a British right-leaning tabloid stereotypically read by middle England.
explanation.definitionFit: Buyers of the conservative tabloid are the stereotype of comfortable, right-leaning middle England.

clue.text: Pudding everyday?

definitions.meaning: a baked British dessert of ... sliced loaf and custard
basic and routine, as in one's staple work

explanation.definitionFit: Add pudding to get a traditional British baked dessert; alone, the idiom means basic, routine and ordinary.
